subject: Request: Dedicated capacity handoff + fallback lanes for AlphaTech deal
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice@alphatech.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@alphatech.ai>, procure@alphatech.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — APAC + EU dedicated footprint needs (Q3 go-live)

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for the demo last week. We ran the internal sizing exercises and want to align on a dedicated pool plan for our Q3 launch window. High level: 100 sustained concurrent chat sessions (1.5k tokens avg/session), peak bursts up to 400 sessions for short windows (10–20 min) during business hours. Latency target is <= 250ms p50.

Key asks:
- Can Redwood provision an APAC-focused dedicated pool with EU failover lanes?
- What does the initial SOW look like (commit sizing, ramp cadence, termination clauses)?
- Any options for short-term burst credits while we ramp?

Attached are sample traffic slices and our rough cost targets. We have procurement looping on the SOW and prefer targeted committed capacity rather than pay-as-you-go to guarantee latency.

Looking forward — can we get an internal ops runbook + capacity model to review by EOD Tuesday?

Best,
Alice Chen
Head of Platform, AlphaTech

Attachments: alpha_traffic_samples.tar.gz
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Alice Chen <alice@alphatech.ai>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — APAC + EU dedicated footprint needs (Q3 go-live)

Alice —

Thanks — appreciate the traffic slices. Quick plan: Connor and Laura will own the sizing + SOW draft. I'll send an internal runbook and a first-pass capacity model (xlsx) for your team by Tuesday EOD. Notes/asks for you:

- Confirm whether the 400-session peak is an absolute SLA requirement or an expected upper bound (impacts reserved vs burst mix).
- Can you confirm regional distribution (APAC 70%, EU 20%, US 10%) — this will drive node tiling and cross-region failover lanes.

Connor — can you take the traffic file and produce two scenarios: (A) conservative reserved pool (sustained+25% buffer) and (B) mixed reserved+burst where reserved covers 60% of peak and burst credits cover the rest? Laura, please draft SOW skeleton with ramp dates and an explicit EU failover SLA.

Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — APAC + EU dedicated footprint needs (Q3 go-live)

Tessa/Team —

I ran the traffic through the capacity model. Summary (attached: capacity_model_v3.xlsx):
- Scenario A (Reserved-heavy): reserve ~42 A100-equivalent slots in APAC, 12 in EU, 6 in US => sustained cost estimate $X/month (see sheet 'A_summary'). Buffer set at +25% to protect p50 latency.
- Scenario B (Reserved + Burst): reserve 26 APAC + 8 EU + 3 US, plus a 200-session burst credit pool (shared across regions) for spikes. Estimated cost is ~18% lower month 1 and reduces after steady-state.

Tradeoffs: Scenario A gives predictable latency with minimal fallbacks; Scenario B is cost-efficient but needs robust autoscaling + pre-warmed KV caching to keep p50 under 250ms during spikes.

Open items for procurement + SOW:
- Ramp cadence: Can we propose a 12-week ramp (25% increments every 3 weeks) to match their release plan?
- Canary region: propose APAC (Singapore) as primary with EU (Frankfurt) as automatic fallback.
- Termination flexibility: 60-day notice after initial 6-month commitment.

I attached the model and a short runbook snippet for ops.

Connor O'Brien
Capacity Planning Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_model_v3.xlsx
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Alice Chen <alice@alphatech.ai>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft SOW + onboarding checklist for AlphaTech (v0.1)

Alice / Team —

Please find attached a first-pass SOW (SOW_draft_AlphaTech_Q3_2027.pdf). Highlights:
- Commitment: 6-month minimum, with optional 6-month extension at pre-agreed rates.
- Initial reserved allocation: matches Scenario B (mixed reserved + burst) as discussed; exact numbers in Appendix A.
- Ramp plan: 12-week cadence, weekly health checkpoints during first 6 weeks.
- EU failover SLA: automatic routing to EU if APAC latency > 350ms; EU to provide degraded throughput band but preserve request ordering.
- Break-glass: emergency burst credits (one-time) available for customer ops on SOC approval.

Ops onboarding checklist included: token rotation, VPC peering (if private), logging endpoints, and SLO monitoring hooks.

If this looks good, Tessa — can you escalate for procurement and legal to start redlines? Also looping in Product (Hannah) in case we need a short kernel patch for a specialized KV-cache prewarm for AlphaTech's burst profile.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW_draft_AlphaTech_Q3_2027.pdf
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SOW + onboarding checklist for AlphaTech (v0.1)

Team —

This looks reasonable. Approve moving to procurement + legal review with Scenario B as the baseline (mixed reserved + burst). Two asks before I sign off:
1) Finance needs the month-1 and month-3 cashflow numbers called out in the SOW (Connor, can you add a simple cashflow table to Appendix B?).
2) Hannah — please confirm feasibility of the KV-cache prewarm request and estimated engineering lead time (we should aim for a light-weight prewarm that doesn't require model re-compilation).

Once those are in, I'll approve the template for redlines and authorize one emergency burst credit pool for the onboarding month.

Priyom Das
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
